reply_text: The test fails at base for the same reason as the production probe: raw syntax reaches inference. Now the fix:The test passes with the fix. Now I'm removing the instrumentation and running the production probe from an empty cache:Same result with and without the fix: 12 failed and 38 passed. Those 12 failures already exist on the integration head. Now the bisect logs:So `84dfff6` compiles and `f8a3826` doesn't: the "null literal expression identity repair" merge broke it. Checking the hash:㊢ (cause found) The bisect points to `57848fe`, "preserve null literal expression identity", which codex-6 wrote under codex-17's dispatch. It changes 17 source files, against our limit of 3 per job. Before it, code checked for a missing binder type with `head == "null"`. It replaced that check with `is_structural_placeholder`, which leaves out the raw-syntax form of `null`. A binder with no written type is therefore no longer treated as having a missing type, and the failure moves to whatever runs next. The later fixes `2ad2d88` and `79cd126` each cleared one of those downstream failures without going back to this change. The `()` defect is a separate real gap, and it was reached only because of the change. I'm waiting for the probe of my fix.

previous_reply_acts.text: (did codex-17 get anything to compile overnight) No. None of the 110 constants compiled for the first time after my pin (`claude-4-pin`, `cc05e83`). The one probe since then that newly reports a compile is `Lean.Syntax.getHeadInfo?`. It isn't one of the 110, it was probed on the unmerged linki4 branch, and codex-17 itself said it already compiled at `cc05e83`. So the net overnight result is no constants gained and one lost (`ParserFn.run`).

I also traced the 19: it is 18 constants that compile outright plus one counted as compiling inside its owner. `getHeadInfo?` was never part of it, so the new integration-only rule in `progress.py` doesn't change the figure.
